candidate.answerReason: Using \(i^2=-1\), the product is \(9-i^2=9+1=10\), matching the supplied key.

methods.label: Conjugate product and modulus
methods.explanation: The factors \(3+i\) and \(3-i\) are conjugates, so their product equals \(|3+i|^2\). The square of the modulus is \(9+1=10\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the standard conjugate-product identity and modulus formula within the stated required course.

methods.label: Difference of squares
methods.explanation:
The factors have the same real term and opposite imaginary terms, so the difference of squares formula applies. Using \(i^2=-1\),
\[
(3+i)(3-i)=3^2-i^2=9+1=10.
\]
methods.levelReason: Uses an earlier algebraic identity and basic complex multiplication without requiring the modulus formula.
